rules.rule: Every spoken line, including the final sentence, must have a caption that stays on screen until the speech ends.
rules.because: She flags any caption gaps, e.g., "Captions missing in 0.16second," so she will also notice missing captions at the close.

rules.rule: All captions must use the same font, size, colour and background throughout the reel.
rules.because: Her focus on caption presence suggests she will also enforce visual uniformity of captions.

rules.rule: Colour grading of every B‑roll clip must match the lighting and tone of the professor’s primary footage throughout the whole reel.
rules.because: She already rejected a single mismatch (“Grading vs delivery not good on the scooter at 0.07”), indicating a broader expectation of consistent grading.

rules.rule: Avoid sudden colour shifts between cuts; transitions should feel seamless.
rules.because: Her comment on grading implies she notices any visual discontinuity that distracts from the delivery.

rules.rule: The professor’s face must remain on screen for at least the first five seconds before any graphics or AI images appear.
rules.because: She stresses opening on the professor’s face before AI elements.

rules.rule: Each reel should have a brief intro, a middle that supports the main point, and a concise wrap‑up that returns to the professor.
rules.because: Her structural feedback (“Open on the professor’s face…”) shows she values a logical flow.

rules.rule: Every visual element (AI image, slide, B‑roll) must illustrate exactly what the professor is saying at that moment.
rules.because: She already flagged mismatched visuals (“visuals not matching what the speaker says”).

rules.rule: Do not use generic stock clips that do not have a clear connection to the spoken content.
rules.because: Her emphasis on relevance suggests she will reject unrelated filler footage.

rules.rule: Animated slide graphics and title cards must fade or slide in gently; abrupt pops are not acceptable.
rules.because: She approves hard cuts but expects professionalism, so jarring animation would stand out.

rules.rule: The professor’s voice should remain at a consistent volume throughout; no sudden drops or spikes.
rules.because: While she hasn’t mentioned audio yet, her attention to detail in visual grading implies she will also notice audible inconsistencies.
